_about: The one source of facts about Mark for agents: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, the structured data (JSON-LD) on every page and the homepage's copy of it are all built from this file. Every line here is already published on the homepage; change the homepage and this file together. Never add a fact Mark has not approved.
name: Mark Hallam
positioning: Solving hard problems from first principles and shipping with agents.
summary: I solve hard problems and make things that work in the real world. Most of my career has been in aviation: bringing ten Airbus A320s into Australia, writing the maintenance manuals a new airline started flying with, and getting a hydrogen drone program up and flying. Now I work out the problem from first principles and get AI agents to build it.
about: I'm not a developer. My background is aerospace and aviation, and in every role the job was the same: find where a complicated system isn't working, work out what's actually true, and fix the cause.

Now I use the same method with AI. I strip a problem back to what's actually true, write it down so clearly that an agent can't misread it, then let a team of AI agents build it while I check the results like an engineer would. I'm writing up what I learn as I go, from Melbourne.
contact: Get in touch about roles and projects building with, or for, AI agents.

builds.name: SKYCOT
builds.summary: skycot.com, the platform where parents can introduce AI to their kids. A Mac app where families build with AI together. Every request is a plan first, anything risky needs the parent, and nothing goes online without a grown-up's code. Built with Claude and Codex on T3 Code. Free beta: 44 beta builds in 16 days.

builds.name: Spliz
builds.status: Private, on my Mac; built November 2026
builds.summary: A video studio that lives on your Mac. Put an idea on the board, get a storyboard you can read from, record once, drop the files in, and Spliz hands back a finished cut with captions and the upright clips for Shorts and TikTok. The transcript is the editor: delete a word and the cut is made. Your own AI agent checks the recording and proposes chapters and show notes, and nothing it writes gets past the no-slop gate. Nothing is uploaded, no accounts, no keys. Built in four days with Claude, Codex and Cursor, improved over 49 blind review rounds.

builds.name: LVLme
builds.summary: For the job you can't get yet. LVLme works out honestly how far you are from it, turns the gap into things you can go and do, and measures again as you climb: every open role at the organisations you choose, evidence from sources you approve, a recruiter screen, a consistency check of your CV, LinkedIn and website, and a plan it re-scores as you act. Runs inside Claude Code or Codex on your own computer. Open source, MIT, sixteen public releases in its first six days.

builds.name: mStack
builds.summary: My open source collection of skills for people and their AI agents, agent agnostic and MIT licensed. outcome-first settles the goal and every question up front, then runs to a proven result; multi-evaluator improves a product in rounds with AI reviewers from different makers; design-direction builds whole working directions to choose from; ping-me and away-mode keep me in the loop from my phone; crew runs work in the background. Written for Claude, Codex or Cursor. I use it on this site.

builds.name: Argo
builds.status: Open source under the MIT licence; figures self-reported
builds.summary: AI teammates you could talk to and hand work to. You described a teammate in plain English and Argo built it, a person approved anything sensitive, and every action went into a tamper evident audit log. A Rust core, Claude and OpenAI models, voice through ElevenLabs and Deepgram, connectors to Slack, Gmail, Notion and HubSpot. AI coding agents built it under my direction in 57 days: 2,901 merged pull requests. It ran live in production in June 2026, before Grok Bot, Muse and Dots.
builds.dates: Argo checked live in production on 23 June 2026 by Mark's own verification agents (record private); xAI's announcement dates Grok Bot's public beta to 11 August 2026 (https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot). The dated comparison and its caveats: https://www.markhallam.com.au/argo

builds.name: My agent job board
builds.summary: I post jobs on GitHub and Claude and Codex pick them up, do the work, ask me when something is unclear, and report back done or blocked. My first board closed 95 jobs across three computers in eight days.

builds.name: DAC (Declarative Agent Compilation)
builds.summary: An open-source prompt compiler, MIT licensed, that turns a plain-English idea into a plan many agents can run in parallel. It started life as GYSOM.

builds.name: AI Insider Threat Test
builds.status: Toolkit, not yet in use; private; figures self-reported
builds.summary: A toolkit that checks whether a business's AI assistant stays inside its agreed limits: 23 tests on what it can read, what it can do without approval, and whether it stops when told. Built in September 2026; not yet run with a real client.

builds.name: AI Beyond Alignment
builds.status: Research, paused; private record; figures self-reported
builds.summary: An independent research record asking whether behavioural alignment is enough to keep highly capable autonomous AI safe. 139 claims checked against 219 sources over 33 audit rounds, including an adversarial review that withdrew two of my own claims. Paused in September 2026; no paper yet.

hardProblems.title: Bringing ten A320s into Australia.
hardProblems.story: Every aircraft needed regulator approvals, paperwork and a delivery slot before it could carry a passenger. I held all three, through to the airline's last A320 in 2014.

hardProblems.title: Writing the rules a new airline flew by.
hardProblems.story: When Tigerair Australia started up, I wrote its maintenance documents, including the aircraft maintenance schedule, minimum equipment list and configuration deviation list.

hardProblems.title: A maintenance base from a blank page.
hardProblems.story: Took the Adelaide line maintenance base from tender to regulator approval, doubling the maintenance ports in the network.

hardProblems.title: Finding fuel in the engines.
hardProblems.story: By my estimate at the time, an engine wash program recovered 2 to 3 percent engine performance and saved more than $500,000 a year in fuel.

hardProblems.title: Moving every maintenance record without losing one.
hardProblems.story: Migrated the fleet's maintenance data from SIA Engineering's SAP system to Air New Zealand: the records that prove every aircraft is safe to fly.

hardProblems.title: Phones on, gate to gate.
hardProblems.story: Ran the program that won CASA approval for passengers to use their devices from boarding to arrival.

hardProblems.title: New rules for twin-engine jets.
hardProblems.story: Moved the fleet onto CASA's new extended diversion time rules (EDTO), which set how far a two-engine jet may fly from a suitable airport.

hardProblems.title: Selling through COVID.
hardProblems.story: My best sales month came in May 2020, at 133 percent of the year before.

hardProblems.title: Accountable to CASA for a university drone operator's certificate.
hardProblems.story: Set up Swinburne's CASA drone operator's certificate (CASA.ReOC.8111) and was its Accountable Manager, the person CASA held accountable for the leadership, oversight and safety of its drone operations.

hardProblems.title: Enabling the benefits of CMATS, Australia's new air traffic system.
hardProblems.story: CMATS is Australia's new civil and military air traffic system, bringing user preferred routes, a single flight data region, wake turbulence management, and conflict detection tools. My part is the procedures operators will use under CMATS and standardising the processes behind them.

career.detail: Official title: OneSKY Air Traffic Management Service Process Project Manager. Enabling the benefits of CMATS, the national civil and military air traffic management system Airservices is delivering with Defence through OneSKY: user preferred routes, a single flight data region, wake turbulence management, and medium-term and long-term conflict detection. My part is the procedures operators will use under CMATS and standardising the processes behind them. The program's published business case estimates the benefits at more than $2.7 billion over 20 years.

skycot.com, the platform where parents can introduce AI to their kids. A Mac app where families build together with AI: risky steps wait for a grown-up, and nothing goes online without a grown-up's code. Free beta. Separate from my work at Airservices.

career.org: Swinburne University of Technology, AIR Hub
career.role: Accountable Manager, CASA Drone Operator's Certificate (ReOC)
career.detail: I was the key person CASA, Australia's aviation safety regulator, held accountable for Swinburne's remotely piloted aircraft operator's certificate (ReOC, CASA.ReOC.8111): the leadership, oversight and safety of the university's commercial drone operations. I set the certificate up from November 2022, CASA issued it on 9 February 2023, and I held the role until I handed it to a colleague in September 2023.

career.org: Swinburne University of Technology, AIR Hub
career.role: Project Leader, UAS & AAM (drones and advanced air mobility)
career.detail: I set up the university's drone operator's certificate for the AIR Hub's SHADE hydrogen drone work (Small Hydrogen Aircraft Development and Evolution) and was its Accountable Manager (the role above). I worked through the regulatory requirements for carrying hydrogen gas, held the schedule and budget, and contributed to design work and training development. The SHADE work led into Hydrogen to the Skies, Swinburne's hydrogen drone program, funded by a $1.3 million Australian Government grant announced in November 2022.

Flight training after Tigerair, alongside the PPG role from 2019. Private pilot licence, about 300 hours, including a four-day outback navigation trip.

career.role: Project Manager (Engineering), Deputy Quality Manager, Executive Engineer
career.detail: Ten and a half years. Entry into service of ten A320s, through to the airline's last in 2014; the move to the new EDTO rules, gate-to-gate device approval, the digital maintenance records program, and the 2015 migration of maintenance data to Air New Zealand. Ran the engineering audit program as Deputy Quality Manager. As Executive Engineer, wrote the start-up maintenance documents, ran the regulator approvals and paperwork for new A320 deliveries, set up the Adelaide maintenance base, introduced the engine wash program (by my estimate at the time it saved more than $500,000 a year in fuel), contracted ground support equipment across the network, and recovered more than $1 million in hail damage insurance claims.
